questions.question: Who is famous for playing the percussion instrument Tabla?

questions.solution: Allah Rakha was a legendary tabla player renowned for his virtuosity and major contributions to Indian classical music. questions.question: In India, the tradition of singing ghazal was established by____________.
questions.questionHtml: In India, the tradition of singing ghazal was established by____________.
questions.solution:
The correct option is Hazrat Amir Khusrau.

Key Points

  • The full name of Hazrat Amir Khusrau was Abu'l Hasan Yamīn ud-Dīn Khusrau.
  • He was an Indo-Persian Sufi singer, musician, poet and scholar who lived under the Delhi Sultanate.
  • He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya of Delhi.
  • He is also known as 'father of Qawwali','Parrot of India' and also referred as 'father of Urdu Literature'.
  • Amir Khusrau was the court poet of Alauddin Khilji.​

Additional Information

  • ​Hazrat Ali was a cousin, son-in-law and companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. He  was killed by ibn Muljam, who wanted revenge for the Battle of Nahrawan.
  • Hazrat Nizamuddin was an sunni muslim scholar, contemporary to  Ghiyas-ud-din tughluq.
  • Hazrat Nizamuddin Aulia was the teacher of Amir Khusrau. His tomb is in Delhi.
  • Hazrat Shahenshahwali also known as Hussain Shah Wali was a sufi saint of Golkonda during the reign of Qutb-Sahi Dynasty. He died in 1620.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of music usually associated with Sufism?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a form of music usually associated with Sufism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Qawwali.

Key Points

  • Qawwali is a form of music usually associated with Sufism.
  • Sufi music is the devotional music of the Sufis, inspired by the works of Sufi poets, like Rumi, Hafiz, Bulleh Shah, Amir Khusrow and Khwaja Ghulam Farid.
  • Qawwali is the best-known form of Sufi music and is most commonly found in the Sufi culture in South Asia. 
  • Sufi love songs are often performed as ghazals and Kafi, a solo genre accompanied by percussion and harmonium, using a repertoire of songs by Sufi poets.
  • The roots can largely be found in Persia, parts of the Arabic world, Pakistan and India.
  • Current Sufi orders include Alians, Bektashi Order, Mevlevi Order, Ba 'Alawiyya, Chishti Order, Jerrahi, Naqshbandi, Mujaddidi, Ni'matullāhī, Qadiriyya, Qalandariyya, Sarwari Qadiriyya, Shadhiliyya, Suhrawardiyya, Saifiah (Naqshbandiah), and Uwaisi.

Additional Information

  • Thumri :
    • Thumri is a vocal genre or style of Indian music.
    • The term "thumri" is derived from the Hindi verb thumakna, which means "to walk with dancing steps so as to make the ankle-bells tinkle." 
    • A ghazal is mainly a poetic form than a musical form, but it is more song-like than the thumri.
  • Khayal :
    • The origins of khayal are often associated with the famous musician Amir Khusrau.
    • The sultans of Jaunpur—notably Mohammad Sharqi and Hussain Sarqi, who were contemporaries of the Mughal emperor Babur—were patrons of musicians who developed khayal.
  • Ghazal
    • A ghazal is a form of amatory poem or ode, originating in Arabic poetry.
    • A ghazal may be understood as a poetic expression of both the pain of loss or separation and the beauty of love in spite of that pain.
    • The ghazal form is ancient, tracing its origins to 7th-century Arabic poetry.

questions.question: Budhaditya Mukharjee, Vilayat Khan and Mustaq Ali Khan are associated with which musical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: Budhaditya Mukharjee, Vilayat Khan and Mustaq Ali Khan are associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sitar.

Key Points

  • Budhaditya Mukherjee is a prominent Sitar player known for his proficiency and contribution to Hindustani classical music.
  • Vilayat Khan was one of the most famous Sitar players and belonged to the Imdadkhani Gharana, known for the Gayaki Ang style of playing.
  • Mustaq Ali Khan was another notable Sitar maestro and was renowned for his Dhrupad style of playing.
  • The Sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, known for its rich tonal quality and complex playing technique.

Additional Information

  • Surbahar
    • Also known as the bass sitar, it is a plucked string instrument used in the Hindustani classical music of North India.
    • It was developed in the 19th century and has a deeper tone compared to the sitar.
    • It is used for playing the slower, more meditative sections of a raga.
  • Sarod
    • A string instrument, used mainly in Indian classical music.
    • It is known for a deep, weighty, introspective sound.
    • It is also known for its characteristic smooth, sliding sound (glissando or meend), produced by the absence of frets.
  • Santoor
    • A hammered dulcimer of Persian descent, it is played with a pair of light wooden mallets.
    • It is a trapezoid-shaped instrument and has multiple strings (usually 72 to 100).
    • The Indian santoor is more rectangular than its Persian counterpart and has more strings.
  • Sitar
    • A plucked stringed instrument, predominantly used in Hindustani classical music.
    • It has a long neck with 20 metal frets and six to seven main strings.
    • It also has 13 sympathetic strings that run underneath the frets and resonate with the played strings, adding to its complex sound.

questions.question: Vilayat Khan is known for playing which of the following instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Vilayat Khan is known for playing which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sitar.

Key Points

Sitar instrument:

  • The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.
  • The instrument was invented in medieval India and flourished in the 16th and 17th centuries and arrived at its present form in 18th-century India.
  • Used widely throughout the Indian subcontinent, the sitar became popularly known in the wider world through the works of Ravi Shankar, beginning in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
  • In the 1960s, a short-lived trend arose for the use of the sitar in Western popular music, with the instrument appearing on tracks by bands such as the Beatles, the Doors, the Rolling Stones, and others.

Additional Information

  • Santoor
    • The santoor is a hammered dulcimer, a trapezoid-shaped instrument with strings that are struck with small mallets.
    • It has its origins in Persia and is a popular instrument in Indian classical music, particularly in the Kashmir region.
    • The santoor typically has 100 strings arranged in groups, and the player uses two small wooden mallets to produce a wide range of sounds and effects.
    • It is known for its delicate and expressive sound, capable of producing both subtle and powerful musical phrases.
    • Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a renowned santoor virtuoso who played a crucial role in popularizing the instrument in Indian classical music.
  • Sarod
    • The sarod is a fretless, long-necked lute that is a prominent instrument in Hindustani classical music.
    • It is characterized by its deep, resonant sound and intricate playing techniques.
    • The sarod has a gourd-shaped body and a long neck with 20 to 25 frets.
    • It is played with a small metal plectrum called a "meend" that allows for subtle variations in pitch and timbre.
    • Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan are two of the most celebrated sarod maestros in the world.
  • Violin
    • The violin is a string instrument with four strings, played with a bow.
    • It is one of the most widely recognized and versatile instruments in Western classical music.
    • The violin has a long history, evolving from earlier bowed instruments like the viol.
    • It is capable of producing a wide range of sounds, from delicate and lyrical to powerful and dramatic.
    • Famous violinists include Niccolò Paganini, Jascha Heifetz, and Itzhak Perlman.

questions.questionHtml: Palghat Raghu was a famous _________ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is mridangam.

Key Points

  • Palghat Raghu was a legendary Indian percussionist known for his expertise in playing the mridangam, a classical Indian percussion instrument.
  • He was born in the Palghat district of Kerala, which is known for producing several renowned mridangam artists.
  • Palghat Raghu received numerous awards and recognitions, including the prestigious Padma Shri from the Government of India in 1985.
  • He was a highly respected figure in Carnatic music circles and collaborated with many distinguished musicians throughout his career.

Additional Information

  • Mridangam
    • The mridangam is a double-headed drum that is an essential component of South Indian classical music (Carnatic music).
    • It is made from a hollowed piece of jackfruit wood and has two drumheads, each producing different pitches.
    • The mridangam is played with the hands, and the musician uses various techniques to produce a wide range of sounds and rhythms.
    • It is considered the primary rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic music, often paired with instruments like the violin, flute, and veena.
  • Other Instruments Mentioned:
    • Sarangi: A bowed, short-necked string instrument from India, used primarily in Hindustani classical music.
    • Flute: A woodwind instrument that produces sound from the flow of air across an opening. In Indian classical music, the bansuri is a popular bamboo flute.
    • Tabla: A pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent, widely used in Hindustani classical music and other genres.

questions.question: Pannalal Ghosh is famous for which musical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: Pannalal Ghosh is famous for which musical instrument?
questions.solution: Pannalal Ghosh is renowned for his mastery of the flute and is credited with introducing it to Indian classical music, significantly elevating its status in this genre. His contributions influenced the playing techniques and repertoire of the flute, including innovations such as extending its length to produce a deeper, richer sound. Born on 31 July 1911 and passing away on 20 April 1960, he is often called the "Father of North Indian Classical Flute." Ghosh's approach was influenced by vocal styles, and he composed several classical pieces and ragas still performed today.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Abdul Karim Khan.

Key Points

  • Abdul Karim Khan was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music.
  • Kirana Gharana is one of the most prominent Indian classical khayal gharanas and is associated mostly with the perfect intonation of notes.
  • The gharana's style was further evolved and was established as one of the important styles in modern Indian classical music in the late 19th /early 20th centuries by the musicians Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan.
  • The name of this school of music comes from Kirana or Kairana, a town and tehsil of Shamli District in Uttar Pradesh.

Additional Information

  • Gharana is a system in which people organize socially that links musicians and dancers.
  • It is an apprenticeship or lineage, for the adherence to a particular musical style.
  • The word Gharana originates from the Urdu/Hindi word 'Ghar", which means 'house' or Family.
  • A Gharana also indicates a comprehensive musicological ideology and differentiates one school from another.
  • Some of the Gharanas well known for singing Hindustani classical music are Agra, Gwalior, Indore, Jaipur, Kirana, and Patiala.

questions.question: Who among the following is the pioneer and founder of Kirana Gharana of Hindustani music?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is the pioneer and founder of Kirana Gharana of Hindustani music?
questions.solution: Abdul Karim Khan is recognized as the pioneer and founder of the Kirana Gharana of Hindustani music, one of the most prominent schools of this genre. His style and teachings significantly influenced the development of Hindustani classical music. Known for his melodious voice and emotional depth, he emphasized the importance of 'swara' (musical note) and aimed for perfect intonation. The Kirana Gharana, named after his birthplace in Uttar Pradesh, includes other notable exponents like Sawai Gandharva, Bhimsen Joshi, and Firoz Dastur, all influenced by Abdul Karim Khan. His legacy is preserved by his disciples and followers.

  • His music style is noted for its emotional depth and technical proficiency, which has inspired many subsequent musicians.
  • The Nadhaswaram itself is a double-reed instrument, similar to the North Indian shehnai but larger and with a more robust sound.
  • Pillai's performances have left a lasting legacy in the field of Carnatic music, and his recordings are still revered today.

questions.question: Which Assamese artist was known as Sudhakantha?

questions.solution: Bhupen Hazarika, known as Sudhakantha or 'The Nightingale', was a celebrated Assamese artist recognized for his profound contributions to music and culture. questions.question: ‘West Meets East’ is an album by American violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Indian sitar virtuoso ________.
questions.questionHtml: ‘West Meets East’ is an album by American violinist Yehudi Menuhin and Indian sitar virtuoso ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ravi Shankar.

Key Points

  • Ravi Shankar was a renowned Indian sitar virtuoso and composer who significantly contributed to popularizing Indian classical music globally.
  • The collaboration between Yehudi Menuhin and Ravi Shankar led to the creation of the album 'West Meets East' in 1967, which was a landmark in the fusion of Western and Eastern musical traditions.
  • Ravi Shankar's influence extended to notable Western musicians, including George Harrison of The Beatles, who studied under him and integrated Indian music into The Beatles' work.
  • Ravi Shankar was awarded several prestigious awards, including Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, for his contributions to music.

Additional Information

  • Yehudi Menuhin
    • Yehudi Menuhin was an American-born violinist and conductor who became one of the most famous violinists of the 20th century.
    • He was known for his exceptional technique, emotional depth, and his efforts to use music to bridge cultural divides.
    • Menuhin's collaboration with Ravi Shankar was part of his broader interest in exploring and incorporating different musical traditions into his work.
  • Indian Classical Music
    • Indian classical music is one of the oldest musical traditions in the world, with origins tracing back over two thousand years.It is broadly divided into two major traditions: Hindustani music (North Indian) and Carnatic music (South Indian).
    • Ravi Shankar was a key figure in Hindustani classical music, known for his mastery of the sitar and his deep understanding of ragas and talas.
  • Fusion Music
    • Fusion music blends elements from different musical genres to create new, hybrid forms.
    • The 'West Meets East' album is a seminal example of fusion music, combining Western classical music with Indian classical music.
    • This genre aims to transcend cultural boundaries and create a universal musical language.

questions.question: In the Hindustani music system, the ________ are allotted to different hours of the day and different seasons.
questions.questionHtml: In the Hindustani music system, the ________ are allotted to different hours of the day and different seasons.
questions.solution: In the Hindustani music system, ragas are designed to be played or sung during specific times of the day or seasons to evoke particular emotions. This tradition enhances the listener's emotional and aesthetic experience and preserves the rich heritage of Indian classical music. Ragas are melodic frameworks for improvisation, each with unique characteristics. Varnas are patterns of notes for teaching and practicing ragas. Gita refers to songs or hymns, while srutis are microtones fundamental to the Indian classical music tuning system, with 22 srutis in an octave.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian Playback Singers holds the Guinness world record for singing the highest number of songs in one day?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following Indian Playback Singers holds the Guinness world record for singing the highest number of songs in one day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kumar Sanu.

Key Points

  • Kumar Sanu
    • Indian playback singer Kedarnath Bhattacharaya, better known by his stage name Kumar Sanu, was born on October 20, 1957.
    • In Bollywood, he is referred to as the King of Melody.
    • Kishore Kumar, a vocalist, has a big impact on the way he sings and sounds.
    • He is well known for singing numerous Bollywood and Hindi songs.
    • In 1993, Kumar Sanu holds the Guinness world record for singing the highest number of songs in one day.
    • He recorded 28 songs in one day.
    • He had received the Best Male Playback Singer Filmfare Award five times in a consecutive manner (1990–1994).
    • He received the Padma Shri honour from the Indian government in 2009 for his contributions to Indian music and film.

Additional Information

  • Along with Hindi, he has performed across Bengal, Bangladesh, as well as West Bengal, singing in Bengali, his home tongue, as well as Marathi, Nepali, Assamese, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Tamil, Punjabi, Bhojpuri, Gujarati, Manipuri, Odia, Chhattisgarhi, Urdu, and Pali.
  • Alka Yagini
    • Indian playback vocalist Alka Yagnik, who was born on March 20, 1966, specialises in Hindi cinema.
    • Numerous awards, including two National Film Awards for Best Female Playback Singer, have been given to Yagnik.
    • The Lata Mangeshkar Award was given to Yagnik in 2017 for her work in the music industry.
  • Kavita Krishnamurthy
    • Sharada is an Indian playback and classical vocalist also known by the name Kavita Krishnamurthy or Kavita Subramaniam.
    • She has recorded more than 50,000 Songs recorded in 46 different languages.
    • She has won the Padma Shri in 2005 and four Filmfare Best Female Playback Singer Awards, which she won consecutively from 1995 to 1997.
